title: SCHADS Level 5 Salary 2026–27: Hourly Rates, Fortnightly Pay and Annual Salary for a 38-Hour Week
description: Find the SCHADS Level 5 salary for 2026–27: hourly rates from $53.43 to $55.85, fortnightly pay, annual salary, tax and super. Based on Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide.
salarySummary: A full-time SCHADS Level 5 employee at pay point 1 earns $53.43 per hour, or $2,030.20 per week for 38 hours, equating to approximately $105,570 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the SCHADS Level 5 salary for 2026–27?
faqs.a: The SCHADS Level 5 hourly rate ranges from $53.43 (pay point 1) to $55.85 (pay point 3) for permanent employees working 38 hours per week. A full-time employee at pay point 1 earns $2,030.20 per week, or about $105,570 per year before tax and super. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the hourly rate $66.79 at pay point 1. These rates are set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026.

faqs.q: How is the SCHADS Level 5 annual salary calculated?
faqs.a: Annual salary is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time SCHADS Level 5 employee at pay point 1 ($53.43 per hour) working 38 hours per week, the annual salary is $53.43 × 38 × 52 = $105,570.40. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances or salary sacrifice. Superannuation is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: What tax and super apply to a SCHADS Level 5 salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, the resident tax scale is: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a SCHADS Level 5 salary of $105,570, tax (including Medicare) would be roughly $24,000–$25,000 depending on your circumstances, and super would be about $12,668.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the SCHADS Level 5 Salary

If you are looking up the **schads level 5 salary**, you are likely working in social or community services under the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award 2010 (SCHADS). The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes a pay guide each year with minimum rates. For 2026–27, the hourly rate for a Level 5 employee ranges from $53.43 to $55.85 depending on your pay point. This article explains how to turn that hourly rate into a weekly, fortnightly and annual figure, and what tax and super you can expect.

### Hourly to Annual: The Basic Formula

The standard way to estimate an annual salary is:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week because that is the ordinary full-time hours under the SCHADS award. For a Level 5, pay point 1 employee:

- Hourly rate: $53.43
- Weekly pay: $53.43 × 38 = $2,030.20
- Fortnightly pay: $2,030.20 × 2 = $4,060.40
- Annual salary: $2,030.20 × 52 = $105,570.40

These figures come from the Fair Work Ombudsman's SCHADS pay guide. The same calculation works for pay point 2 ($54.58/hour → $2,073.91/week → $107,843/year) and pay point 3 ($55.85/hour → $2,122.13/week → $110,351/year).

### Casual Loading and Penalty Rates

If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. That means the casual hourly rate for Level 5 pay point 1 is $66.79. The annual equivalent for a casual working 38 hours every week would be $66.79 × 38 × 52 = $132,000, but casuals do not receive paid leave. The loading compensates for that.

Penalty rates also apply for weekend and public holiday work. For example, a permanent Level 5 employee working a Saturday shift earns $80.15 per hour (150% of the base rate). A typical week with a Saturday shift can push the weekly total to $2,284.18, as shown in the [pay guides](/blog) on this site.

### How the SCHADS Level 5 Salary Compares

The SCHADS Level 5 salary is well above the National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week). It is also higher than many professional awards. For comparison, a Level 5 medical research employee under the Professional Employees Award 2020 earns $59.05 per hour, but that is a different classification. The SCHADS Level 5 rate includes an Equal Remuneration Order adjustment that has been built into the award rates since 2012.

### Tax and Super on a SCHADS Level 5 Salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:
- Tax-free threshold: $0 – $18,200
- 15%: $18,201 – $45,000
- 30%: $45,001 – $135,000
- 37%: $135,001 – $190,000
- 45%: above $190,000

For a $105,570 annual salary, the estimated tax (including the 2% Medicare levy) is roughly $24,500. This is a guide only; your actual tax depends on your circumstances. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary at 12% of ordinary earnings (the super guarantee rate for 2026–27). For a $105,570 salary, that is $12,668 in super contributions, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost for your employer.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a SCHADS Level 5 employee at pay point 1, the fortnightly gross pay is $4,060.40. After tax and Medicare, you might take home around $3,200–$3,300 per fortnight, depending on your tax file number declaration and any other deductions. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site can help you check different scenarios.

### Important Notes

- These rates are minimum award rates. If your employer has an enterprise agreement, different rates may apply.
- The annual figure assumes you work 38 hours every week for 52 weeks. In practice, you may have unpaid leave or shift variations.
- Casual loading and penalty rates are separate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the [timesheet](/) – use the base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax estimates use the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge and salary packaging are not included.

For more details on award classifications and pay points, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool.
